item.title: Separable models of an NIP Banach space theory
item.description: arXiv:2611.33260v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $Y$ be the renorming of $\ell_2(\mathbb N)\oplus_2\ell_2(\mathbb N)$ with norm $(h^2+q^2)^{1/2}$, where $h$ is the Hilbert norm and $q(u,v)=\sup_{i<j}|u_i+v_j|$. We prove that the unstable theory $\operatorname{Th}(Y)$ is NIP in the pure Banach language. We recover the index order from the Banach norm and classify the continuum many separable models up to surjective linear isometry. The invariants are the order type of a countable model of $\operatorname{Th}(\mathbb N,<)$ and the dimension of a separable Hilbert summand. Every such pair occurs. We describe all elementary embeddings between these models. The bounded norm types over a separable model are separable in the uniform metric exactly when its index order contains no copy of $(\mathbb Q,<)$.
item.dc:creator: Karim Khanaki, Pedro Poitevin

item.title: A Sequent Calculus for the Quantified Reflection Calculus $\mathrm{QRC}_1$: Cut-Elimination, Interpolation, and NP-Completeness
item.description: arXiv:2611.33345v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce $\mathrm{G3QRC}_1$, the first Gentzen-style sequent calculus for Borges and Joosten's Quantified Reflection Calculus ($\mathrm{QRC}_1$). As a strictly positive, first-order modal logic, $\mathrm{QRC}_1$ crucially escapes Vardanyan's $\Pi^0_2$-completeness theorem for quantified provability logic, while remaining arithmetically complete with respect to Peano and Heyting Arithmetic. The central innovation of $\mathrm{G3QRC}_1$ is a pair of context-erasing modal rules that simultaneously account for the monotonicity and transitivity axioms by deliberately discarding parametric context across modal boundaries. This structural bottleneck allows for a clean proof of cut-admissibility via a standard lexicographic induction, circumventing the complex loop-checking typically required for provability logics. Cut admissibility yields an instantiated subformula property and supports a direct canonical proof of the finite model property. We streamline the adequate Kripke semantics by interpreting constants globally. We also establish a split-context Craig interpolation theorem and a contextual form of left uniform interpolation, uniformly eliminating private predicate symbols, constants, and free parameters. Finally, by leveraging the rigid structural constraints of the context-erasing rules and the absence of left-branching connectives, we prove that, over the standard fixed countable signatures specified in the paper, the decision problem for $\mathrm{QRC}_1$ is $\mathbf{NP}$-complete, situating this quantified modal logic in a comparatively low nondeterministic complexity class.
item.dc:creator: Mitar Nedeljkovi\'c

item.title: Stability in abstract classes via set theoretic techniques
item.description: arXiv:2611.33530v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that all abstract classes equipped with an independence relation satisfying a mild local character condition are stable. We obtain the result by using methods from model theory and set theory. We have several applications in the context of abstract classes of modules. In particular, we prove that if $K$ is a class of $R$-modules closed under isomorphisms and pure submodules and $\lambda^{\operatorname{card}(R) + \aleph_0} = \lambda$, then $K$ equipped with pure embeddings is stable in $\lambda$.
item.dc:creator: Jeremy Beard, Marcos Mazari-Armida

item.title: A family of forcings with hyperfinite equivalence of generics
item.description: arXiv:2611.34109v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We identify a class of forcings that includes several classical forcings and prove that for all forcings $\mathbb{P}$ in this class the associated equivalence of generics relation $\equiv^{\mathbb{P}}_M$, as defined by Smythe, is a hyperfinite CBER.
item.dc:creator: Ben De Bondt

item.title: Well-foundedness of the strict Lipschitz order on countably complete filters
item.description: arXiv:2611.34850v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In $\mathsf{ZF}+\mathsf{DC}$, the strict Lipschitz order on proper countably complete filters on any fixed ordinal is well-founded. The proof uses transfinite recursion and closure under countable intersections to derive a contradiction from a descending chain. Restricting each filter to the least ordinal it contains yields a set-like well-founded order that compares filters on different ordinals. In $\mathsf{ZF}$, two ultrafilters on the same ordinal are equal if each is nonexpansively reducible to the other. These results answer both parts of Question 9.2.11 in The Ultrapower Axiom.
item.dc:creator: Gabriel Fernandes, Matheus Duzi

item.title: Higher-Dimensional Automata in Geometric Logic
item.description: arXiv:2611.33838v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: What does the topos of a higher-dimensional automaton know about its infinite behaviour that its language does not? We write partial HDAs with an infinite run as models of a geometric theory over an intuitionistic metatheory with no choice. The topos of a machine is that of sheaves on its prefixes. The label word of a prefix records the shape and acceptance bit of each cell with the ipomset of each step. Under unique choice these words give a geometric morphism to the label topos of sheaves on label words, which thus records the shapes and acceptance bits that the B\"uchi language forgets. Machines sharing their B\"uchi language and their frames can differ over the label topos. The bouquet of two squares shares its frame and its B\"uchi language with the interleaved square; each accepted run of either reads the two events in parallel forever. Only the interleaved square has runs through cells of shape a, and the geometric sequent excluding such runs separates the two over the label topos. Over alphabets with decidable equality, finite rigid machines are unambiguous exactly when their label maps are inclusions of locales, and their equivalence over the label topos is decided whenever either is unambiguous. Equivalences of frames over the label topos transport points with their labels, and the invariants of fibres and of the language of points follow from this transport. On finite partial HDAs over alphabets with decidable equality, Muller and B\"uchi acceptance coincide exactly under a weak form of excluded middle.
item.dc:creator: Kenan Oggad

item.title: From Numbers to Container Strings
item.description: arXiv:2411.15873v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We examine two ways of coding sequences in arithmetical theories. We investigate under what conditions they work. To be more precise, we study the creation of objects of a data-type that we call container strings, roughly sequences where the components are ordered but where we do not have an explicitly given projection function and length function. The first coding idea is Smullyan coding and the second one is Markov coding. This second idea is based on the representation of binary strings in the special linear monoid of the non-negative part of discretely ordered commutative rings. We employ Markov coding to obtain an alternative proof that the weak theory ${\sf PA}^-$ is sequential. We prove a correspondence result for a principle for container strings to Euclidean Division under the Markov translation.
item.dc:creator: Albert Visser

item.title: The Uniform Functional Interpretation with Informative Types
item.description: arXiv:2508.12781v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We discuss a new approach to functional interpretations based on uniform quantification and relativization. The uniform quantification in the background permits a more penetrating analysis of principles related to collection and contra-collection. Relativization comes from a computationally informative notion of being an element of a given type. The approach is flexible. When the information takes the shape of bounds, we can recapture a form of the combination of G\"odel's functional {\em dialectica} interpretation with majorizability. When the information is "canonical" in function types, we obtain new functional interpretations and new models of G\"odel's theory T.
item.dc:creator: Fernando Ferreira, Paulo Oliva

item.title: Post Completeness in Conditional Logic
item.description: arXiv:2607.21320v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A logic is Post complete if it is consistent but has no consistent proper extensions. In this article, we systematically investigate Post completeness in conditional logic. We establish some results on the structure of various lattices of conditional logics and examine Post completeness from this perspective. We identify all of the finitely many regular and normal Post complete conditional logics, and prove analogues of Makinson's embedding theorems for certain proper subfamilies of normal conditional logics. We also show that the analogue of Makinson's embedding theorem fails for normal conditional logic by producing an incomplete normal system. Furthermore, we show that certain basic conditional logics have uncountably many Post complete extensions for which closure under some, but not necessarily all, rules peculiar to the conditional are relaxed. Finally, we reflect on what our results tell us about the structure of certain lattices of conditional logics and their connections with modal logic.
item.dc:creator: Giuliano Rosella, Yale Weiss

item.title: On the Definability of Strong Negation in Bilateral Logics
item.description: arXiv:2607.27252v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Recent work in bilateral logic has concerned itself with whether and to what extent strong negation, which "toggles" between assertion and denial, is definable in bilateral systems that lack it. This paper presents a number of results about the definability of strong negation in bilateral systems. First, I show that a constructive Nelson-style Sheffer stroke defines the strong negation of A as (A|(A|A))|A. The same stroke defines the constructive Nelson implication, thus providing a single-connective basis for the strong-negation-and-implication fragment of N4. Second, I provide an exhaustive characterization of the eight combinations of a single "aggregative" connective and a single Nelson-style connective that suffice to jointly define strong negation, with neither defining it individually. One such combination is the material conditional together with constructive co-implication. Third, I show that a constructive and connexive Wansing-style Sheffer stroke (recently referred to as "connexive exclusion") likewise defines the strong negation of A as (A|(A| A))|A and also defines connexive implication. Fourth, I show that, unlike with the Nelson-style connectives, there are no combinations of Wansing-style and aggregative connectives that jointly define strong negation if neither connective defines it individually.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Simonelli

item.title: Stoic Logic and Natural Term Logic
item.description: arXiv:2609.20665v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we propose a reconstruction of Stoic Logic focused on the aspect of multiple generality using the Natural Term Logic (NTL) developped by the author in \cite{ntl}. It can be shown, based on the available evidence, that Stoic logic was far more than a mere propositional logic (we cannot simply identiify the Stoic conditional with propositional conditionals). Its more general and complex logical theory - and notable the treatment of multiple generality - was rather patterned after the logico-syntactic mechanisms of natural language (subject to a regimentation which recalls Polish notation). NTL is likewise is a variable-free formal framework which captures the core syntactic and logic mechanisms of natural language (and notably a large array of features involving intensionality and anaphoric constructions). Bobzien and Shogry \cite{bobzienshogry} have argued that quantified conditionals and multiple generality were treated by the Stoics through a disambiguifying regimentation of syntax using indefinite pronouns and anaphoric constructions involving such pronouns. We contend that the quantified condition expressed through an anaphoric construction involving indefinite pronouns is the fundamental building block of ancient logic. And we explore some possible building blocks for a formal reconstruction of the Stoic logic of universal conditionals (and its corresponding general form of Stoic modus ponens attested by ancient authors) based on NTL. More specifically, we present a version of NTL in which the anaphoric constructions of the Stoic quantified conditional correspond to a type of primitive constructor. The constructor also has a remarkable graph-theoretic interpretation which gives this version of NTL interest in its own right.
item.dc:creator: Clarence Lewis Protin

item.title: Preserving Ramsey ultrafilters with tree forcings
item.description: arXiv:2611.23713v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We define a wide class of tree forcings that we call $\textit{normed-tree forcings}$ and prove that they can preserve Ramsey ultrafilters. These include $\textit{fat-tree forcings}$ as particular cases. As an application, we prove the consistency with $\mathsf{ZFC}$ of $\mathfrak{d}=\mathfrak{u}=\aleph_1 < \mathsf{minLc}=\mathfrak{c}=\aleph_2$, where $\mathfrak{d}$ denotes the dominating number, $\mathfrak{u}$ the ultrafilter number, and $\mathsf{minLc}$ the minimum localization cardinal. This solves some open questions about pairs of classical cardinal characteristics, such as the consistency of both $\mathfrak{e}_{\mathsf{ubd}}$ and its dual strictly larger than $\mathfrak{u}$.
item.dc:creator: Diego A. Mej\'ia, Ulises Ariet Ramos-Garc\'ia

item.title: Propositional Dynamic Logic has Craig Interpolation: a tableau-based proof
item.description:
arXiv:2503.13276v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that Propositional Dynamic Logic (PDL) has the Craig Interpolation Property. This question has been open for many years. Three proof attempts were published, but later criticized in the literature or retracted. Our proof is based on the main ideas from Borzechowski (1988, master thesis). We define a cyclic tableau system for PDL with a loading mechanism to recognize successful repeats. For this system, we show soundness and completeness via a game.
To show interpolation, we modify Maehara's method to work for tableaux with repeats: we first define pre-interpolants at each node, and then use a quasi-tableau to define interpolants for clusters (strongly connected components). In different terms, our method solves the fixpoint equations that characterize the desired interpolants, and the method ensures that the solutions to these equations can be expressed within PDL.
The proof is constructive and we show how to compute interpolants. We make available a Haskell implementation of the proof system that provides interpolants, and a formal verification of our proof in the interactive theorem prover Lean. Lastly, we discuss several questions for future work.
item.dc:creator: Manfred Borzechowski, Malvin Gattinger, Helle Hvid Hansen, Revantha Ramanayake, Francisco Trucco Dalmas, Yde Venema

item.title: Locatedness, Convexity, and Lebesgue Measurability - a New Development
item.description: arXiv:2607.15558v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Set within Bishop's framework for constructive analysis, this paper contains a radically improved and expanded development of material, first published in 1988, dealing with the link between locatedness and Lebesgue measurability for convex subsets of R^{N}.
item.dc:creator: Douglas S Bridges

item.title: A Syntactic Approach to Ulmer's Bialgebras
item.description: arXiv:2607.19587v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Ulmer proposed to view a bialgebraic structure on an object $x$ as a structure map $f\colon Fx\to Gx$ satisfying an equation $\alpha_{(x,f)} = \beta_{(x,f)}$ of natural transformations. This perspective is powerful enough to account for many algebraic and coalgebraic structures, such as varieties of universal algebra, categories of algebras over a PROP, an operad or a monad. We develop Ulmer's bialgebras within a $2$-categorical setting with PIE limits, where structure maps are abstracted by inserters and their equations by equifiers. A syntax of signatures, theories and models is then used to produce these bialgebraic structures. The syntax of the commutative diagrams defining Hopf algebras can be used, as is, to define the $0$-cell of Hopf algebras within any symmetric pseudomonoid in a $2$-category with PIE limits. In this setting, we show that lax morphisms of models induce morphisms between the objects of algebras, extending the classical result lifting a lax monoidal functor to a functor between the categories of internal monoids. Since the construction of the object of bialgebras is expressed entirely in terms of PIE limits, we show that Kan extensions, accessibility, local presentability, orthogonal factorization systems, regularity, and Barr-exactness lift along the construction under suitable assumptions. A bi-dense class of objects allows us to transfer monadicity and local presentability results to formal settings. Finally, we construct a bi-dense class of $\V$-categories with at most three objects, where $\V$ is any monoidal category with an absorbing initial object.
item.dc:creator: David Forsman

item.title: Matrix ultraproducts have trivial fundamental group
item.description: arXiv:2611.18328v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that every tracial ultraproduct $\prod_{\mathcal{U}} M_n(\mathbb{C})$ of matrix algebras has trivial fundamental group. In particular, this establishes that there are uncountably many nonisomorphic matrix ultraproducts, answering a question of Sorin Popa. We actually prove the stronger result that every matrix ultraproduct has trivial first-order fundamental group and thus our techniques are model-theoretic in nature.
item.dc:creator: Hiroshi Ando, Isaac Goldbring

item.title: Littlestone Dimension and Its Dual
item.description: arXiv:2611.26721v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The dual Littlestone dimension of a concept class $\mathcal{H}\subseteq\{0,1\}^{\mathcal{X}}$, $\operatorname{Ldim}^*(\mathcal{H}):=\operatorname{Ldim}(\mathcal{H}^*)$, is the Littlestone dimension of the dual class $\mathcal{H}^*$, obtained by exchanging the roles of domain points and hypotheses. A classical result of Shelah implies that $\operatorname{Ldim}(\mathcal{H})$ and $\operatorname{Ldim}^*(\mathcal{H})$ are finite simultaneously, and quantitative results of Hodges [Mathematika, 1981] imply the doubly exponential bound $\operatorname{Ldim}(\mathcal{H})\le 2^{2^{O(\operatorname{Ldim}^*(\mathcal{H}))}}$. Malliaris and Moran [Trans. Amer. Math. Soc., 2024] asked whether this bound is optimal. We answer this by proving the bound \[ \operatorname{Ldim}(\mathcal{H})\le 2^{O(\operatorname{Ldim}^*(\mathcal{H}))}, \] which is tight up to the constant in the exponent, as witnessed by the class of all binary hypotheses on a finite domain.
item.dc:creator: Pooya Hatami, Chavdar Lalov
